items.title: India’s Biggest Hotel Chain Is Following Its Biggest Travelers
items.summary: You can only build so many Tajs. Scaling to 700 hotels means following demand and building for India's expanding middle class, where consistency matters as much as luxury, rather than chase the shrinking pool of ultra-premium international arrivals.

items.title: Who Owns Your Passport Expiry Date?
items.summary: The travel industry has owners for issuance, verification, and conversion. The missing layer is readiness, and the traveler owns the failure.

items.title: Mews Cuts 15% of Staff, Points to AI in Broad Restructuring — Exclusive
items.summary: Mews says AI can remove the handoffs that once slowed work and hurt margins. Now it has to prove a leaner structure can bring hotels closer, not leave them with less.

items.title: China’s Tongcheng Travel Bids for Dida to Bring Ride-Sharing In-House
items.summary: Chinese OTAs have long offered airport transfers and chauffeur services through third-party partnerships. If completed, Tongcheng's Dida acquisition would make it one of the first to own the ride-sharing marketplace itself, rather than plugging into someone else's.

items.title: Hilton Opens Direct Line to Navan, Cutting Out Corporate Travel Middlemen
items.summary: Hilton and Navan have launched a direct booking connection that skips distribution middlemen, giving the hotel group more control over retailing. It's an early step in a broader corporate travel push to overhaul how road warriors book hotels.
